entry='''### Improve init and add rename and delete subcommands

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A workspace's name is written into six places, and nothing renames or
removes them together: the work-repo's directory, the agent-repo's directory when it is not
nested, the two repos on the remote, each repo's `origin` URL, the `.vc-config.{toml|md}` of both
sides, and the Claude Code symlink. And `init` makes a workspace it cannot always finish, or that
Claude Code does not find.

- The order is wink's: `init` is fixed first, then `vc-x1 delete`, then `vc-x1 rename`. Each is a
  cycle of its own.
- Delete is ahead of rename: its "find every part of a workspace from its config" is what rename
  reuses, and it gives `init` the cleanup it lacks.
- The parts are `####` headings, where [Todo format](agent-data/notes.md#todo-format) asks for
  bullets with a bold title, since a heading is an anchor a link can name.
- Delete leans on two entries far down this list: the clean verdict of [status prints a verdict
  per repo and exits with a bit per
  side](#status-prints-a-verdict-per-repo-and-exits-with-a-bit-per-side), and [status reports the
  commits no bookmark reaches](#status-reports-the-commits-no-bookmark-reaches). Whether they move
  up ahead of it, or delete's cycle builds the verdict as its first rung, is open.
- Two experiments want wink starting fresh Claude Code sessions, the symlink's below and the
  lock's, and can share a sitting.

'''

rest='''#### delete removes a workspace from this machine

- It removes the directories and the symlink, and leaves the remote alone. A repo on the remote
  is deleted by hand.
- Its prompt lists what goes and the commits that are nowhere else.
- What stops it is below.

#### rename renames a workspace, its remote included

- It renames the repos on the remote too. The remote cannot be lost by it: the remote's rename
  happens or is refused, so the repo is under the old name or the new one.
- The remote goes first, so a refusal (the name taken, no permission) leaves the local side as it
  was. The order after it: both `origin` URLs, the configs, a commit and push in both repos, the
  directory, the symlink.
- The new name is checked as [init refuses a name GitHub would
  change](#init-refuses-a-name-github-would-change) checks one, so the URL written is the name
  the remote took.
- A run that stopped between the two repos is run again: it finds which repo has the new name
  and goes on from there.
- A workspace with no remote skips the remote steps. A remote that is not GitHub's is refused.
- Left out, and listed by the command: the name as the family's other repos hold it, the
  template, the messages, and the other members' configs.
- Open: whether it takes the workspace whole or one side at a time. One side alone overlaps
  [repos.agent becomes repos.agent-dir, and a command brings a config up to
  date](#reposagent-becomes-reposagent-dir-and-a-command-brings-a-config-up-to-date).
- Open: whether `.vc-config.toml` is still a form the commands handle.

#### What stops delete and rename

- An agent running in the workspace refuses, by the lock below.
- Uncommitted work, or unpushed work on a bookmark, refuses. This is the status verdict, called
  and not written again. The agent-repo's `@` is clean only after the session exits and a
  `squash-push`.
- Two findings warn and need a yes, `--yes` on the command line or `Y` at the prompt, an agent
  with no terminal using the flag as it does for push:
  - Commits no bookmark reaches.

content.text:
In this project it means commit and push. `AGENTS.md` says so under "Committing vs pushing": "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`, and a local-only save has to be asked for by name as a bare `jj commit`.

The suggested prompt itself comes from Claude Code's interface, not from the project's rules, so it does not know that convention. Typing it here would still get the project's meaning.

What "commit the TODO.md changes" would set off under the rules:

- **A single-step cycle.** Nothing is committed on `main` directly, so it needs a topic bookmark, created and published with your approval.
- **The per-rung flow.** Validation, then "please review" on the diff, then the title and body for your approval, then the push.
- **Land.** `main` moves only when you give the go to land it.

Two things the prompt leaves out:

- **`zDOING.md` changed too.** Its continuation notes were reset to `_None._`, so the commit would carry both files.
- **It would be a docs-only cycle.** The alternative is to let the next cycle's opening carry these edits, which saves a cycle but mixes today's backlog changes into that cycle's first commit.

The plain version: here "commit" always means commit and push through `vc-x1 push`, and for these edits that means a small cycle of its own with the usual reviews and approvals.

112	## The In Progress block
113	
114	A cycle's record, `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, written at the opening
115	([Opening](../AGENTS.md#opening)), finalized and moved to `## Closed` by the closing commit, and
116	deleted by the next opening ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)). The picked-up `## Todo`
117	item is moved here (never copied) and becomes the cycle-record's **provisional items**, all
118	required, all revised as rungs land. The title is a heading one level below `## In Progress` and the
119	other five are headings one level below the title (a plain cycle: `###` title, `####` items, and
120	under a program heading, each one deeper):
121	
122	- **title**, the cycle's name, what `git log --grep` finds it by
123	- **problem statement**: what is wrong, a sentence or two
124	- **solution statement**: what will be done about it, broad. Provisional, and the close-out's commit
125	  body carries the final one
126	- **acceptance check**: the measure of "are you finished?", specific enough that a reader can run
127	  it. Not the per-commit validation, which asks whether the artifact still works. A changed check is
128	  one of the things the deliberation exists to justify
129	- **deliberation**: how the other five were decided, one bullet per decision. The bullet's lead
130	  names the decision and its sentence states it, and the sub-bullets carry the reasons, the
131	  alternatives weighed, and the costs accepted, so a reader can skim the decisions and read the
132	  reasons only where they doubt one. `_None._` when there was nothing to deliberate, which is a real
133	  answer
134	- **ladder**: one rung per step, `- [<title>][M]` plus `(current)` / `(done)`, with `[M]: #<slug>`
135	  in the file's `# References`. The markers stay when the block moves to `## Closed`. `<title>` is
136	  the rung's commit title, `<type>: <desc>` per
137	  [Conventional-commit shape](prose.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit), so a moved
138	  `## Todo` entry is retitled. The closing rung, `<cycle title> closing`, is linked like the rest
139	
140	The ladder heads the **rung subsections**, one per rung under it, the closing included, headed by
141	the rung's exact title, so the ladder is their index. Each opens at laddering with an abstract-sized
142	intent statement (the rung's problem and solution in a sentence or two) and completes at the rung's
143	landing with the conceptual delta: design points, consequences, deferrals, never a restatement of
144	the landed commit body. The closing rung's opens with the stub "Closing out the cycle." and
145	completes at close-out with what closing taught, in problem/solution form, or `_None._`.
146	
147	A rung is `- [<title>][M] (marker)` and carries no detail beyond that: the title links to the rung's
148	subsection. A step is identified by its title (prose.md's [Steps are named, not
149	numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)), so a title carries no number, no version, and no
150	SHA. The version-of-record still bumps for every rung and its suffix still encodes the stage, but
151	that encoding belongs to the manifest and appears nowhere in prose.
152	
153	A single-step cycle's ladder is one unlinked rung, `- <cycle title> (marker)`, with no subsection
154	under it: a subsection headed by the title would collide with the title heading's anchor ([Cycle
155	shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).
156	
157	The block is the cycle's only record. A design finding that must outlive the cycle goes into a
158	`notes/` file by the rung that made it ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)).

236	### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / commit)
237	
238	([why](rationale.md#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit))
239	
240	A ladder step and its commit description share a *title* shape, a [Conventional
241	Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`, an optional
242	`(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail. They differ in
243	the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
244	form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
245	above). The shared template:

the title's marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies take the [Commit-body
form](#commit-body-form), the ladder's are conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface"
above). The shared template:

```
<title>                          # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`

111	## vc-x1 push: what it does and does not do
112	
113	`vc-x1 push <bookmark> --yes --title "..." --body "..."` commits both repos with the approved title
114	and body (`--yes` because push's gates need a tty the agent sandbox lacks, and the user's approval
115	of the shown title and body already covers them), stamps each new commit's `ochid:` trailer
116	([above](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), pushes the work bookmark, and squash-pushes the agent
117	repo's `main`. Three behaviors to keep in mind:
118	
119	- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 runs no build or tests. Validation is the per-rung
120	  flow's job, run *before* the push. The one check that remains is `push-work` verifying the
121	  bookmark's remote refs are tracked.
122	- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume: every stage no-ops when its work is
123	  already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If push exits after `push-work` but before
124	  the agent-repo publish, `vc-x1 squash-push -R <agent-dir>` by hand is the rest of it.
125	- **`ochid:` trailers are stamped by push** ([No hand-written
126	  trailers](#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)), never hand-written into `--title` or `--body`.
127	- **The agent-repo is a linear journal.**
128	  - One push is one agent-repo commit on its `main`, paired with the work-repo commit, whatever
129	    bookmark the work-repo is on.
130	  - Never create an agent-repo bookmark mirroring a work-repo one: it steers session pushes at
131	    the wrong remote ref.
132	- **Squash-push again if `@` is non-empty** after a pass.
133	  - The agent keeps writing session data while the command runs, so its own record lands after
134	    the squash.
135	  - Session data is append-only, so a re-run never conflicts.
136	  - A single pass is never guaranteed to leave `@` empty.
137	
138	A late work-repo tweak after the push (a forgotten edit) needs `jj squash --ignore-immutable` and a
139	re-push, which is a remote rewrite and takes approval like any push.
140	
141	## Re-describing: coordinate first, and keep the trailer
142	
143	**Never `jj describe` a commit that is already published or already carries trailers without
144	coordinating with everyone involved first**
145	([why](rationale.md#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer)). It is a history rewrite,
146	and it silently drops the cross-repo link. Describing a fresh local commit that has never been
147	described and carries no trailers is authoring a message rather than rewriting one, and is not
148	covered. That is a [local
149	ladder](../AGENTS.md#local-ladders)'s scratch describe.
150	
151	When a re-describe is agreed, copy any `ochid:` trailers into the new body by hand (the "don't
152	hand-write trailers" rule covers push authoring a message from scratch, not preserving one already
153	stamped). Hit at a coordinated amend (2026-07-29), where the trailer survived only that way.
154	`vc-x1 fix-desc` repairs a dropped one by title match.
155	
156	## Cycle bookmarks: create and land
157	
158	The mechanics behind [Cycles run on a bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark). That section
159	holds the rule and when it applies, and this one holds the commands
160	([why](rationale.md#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land)).
161	
162	**Create**, at the cycle's opening, with the bookmark named by the cycle title's slug (the anchor
163	algorithm in [Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links), so the block's title heading
164	and the bookmark derive from one bare title):
165	
166	- `jj git push --named <bookmark>=@- -R .` is the common case: it creates the bookmark at the last
167	  committed change and publishes it in one invocation.
168	- Any other revision works as the `=<rev>` right-hand side. When `<rev>` is not `@-`, follow with
169	  `jj new <rev> -R .` so the working copy actually sits on the new line. Otherwise the bookmark
170	  exists and the next commit lands somewhere else.
171	- `jj bookmark set <bookmark> -r <rev> -R .` creates it without publishing, for a line that is not
172	  ready to be seen.
173	
174	**Land**, once the close-out is approved: the sequence that makes the cycle permanent. Every
175	`jj git push` in it is a push under [Approval per push](../AGENTS.md#before-any-push) and [Hard
176	stop after the final push](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push), its own approval, the
177	closing words before the final invocation, silence after ([At
178	rest](../AGENTS.md#at-rest-push-stop-squash-push)):
179	
180	1. Restore the plain name, when the project renamed ([Dev artifact
181	   name](versioning.md#dev-artifact-name)): rename `<name>-dev` back to `<name>` in the manifest,
182	   `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and `jj squash` folds the edit into the closing
183	   (`@` sits directly above it).
184	2. Reshape per the recorded choice: trapezoid runs the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe),
185	   keep separate needs nothing. A single-step cycle has no choice recorded and its one commit lands
186	   as it is.
187	3. Fast-forward: `jj bookmark set main -r <closeout> -R .`, then `jj git push --bookmark main -R .`.
188	   This push publishes the reshaped commit, so the topic bookmark itself is never re-pushed.
189	4. Install: promote the artifact from `main`, the cycle's last act, run when nothing can enter the
190	   cycle anymore.
191	5. Delete the bookmark, locally and remotely: `jj bookmark delete <bookmark>`, then
192	   `jj git push --bookmark <bookmark>` ([Bookmark per
193	   cycle](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)). The long-lived case below gets the same
194	   disposal once fully merged.
195	
196	- The fast-forward needs no `--allow-backwards`. Needing it means the bookmark is not a descendant
197	  of `main`, and the situation wants a look, not a flag.
198	- Landing is the moment the cycle's commits become permanent. No record cites their SHAs
199	  ([Cycle-record](../AGENTS.md#cycle-record)): the landed commits are the record.
200	
201	**Reshape**, while the bookmark is a draft ([Cycles run on a
202	bookmark](../AGENTS.md#cycles-run-on-a-bookmark)):
203	
204	- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
205	  `jj describe`, so [No re-describe without
206	  coordinating](#re-describing-coordinate-first-and-keep-the-trailer) stays intact.
207	- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
208	- **Exceptions**, named and moved past: the bookmark has already landed, another branch is stacked
209	  on it, or the ladder is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

85	## Recording the version-of-record
86	
87	Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
88	case that fits your medium:
89	
90	- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
91	  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and surfaced, and how often it changes. Pick the
case that fits your medium:

- **Manifest**, where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, ...).
    Add the case as needed
- **Notation**, how the `-` form is stored. See [Grammar and storage](#grammar-and-storage):
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`), store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python project), remap to `+`, so `0.3.0-5.3.0`
    becomes `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter**, how a built artifact surfaces the version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence**, how often to bump: see [Unique per
  commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement). This project follows the per-commit
  preference.

## Dev artifact name

When other projects consume the built artifact (e.g. the installed CLI) while this repo is under
active development, the dev build installs under a separate name so a mid-cycle install never
clobbers the binary consumers are running:

- **Name**: the manifest's package name carries a `-dev` suffix (`<name>` -> `<name>-dev`). If Rust,
  `[package].name`, so the per-commit flow's `cargo install` produces `<name>-dev` and leaves plain
  `<name>` untouched.
- **Constant, not per-step**: the step already lives in the version-of-record (`<name>-dev -V`
  reports the exact rung). A per-step name would churn the manifest every commit and litter the
  install dir with stale binaries.
- **Promotion**: plain `<name>` updates only by an explicit act: a separate clone built at the
  chosen commit with the plain name (or a copy of the dev binary), never by the per-commit flow's
  install.

**Single-name variant**: a repo striving to release makes the package name the binary's name, plain
`<name>` on `main` only:

- **The opening renames**: its bump sets `<name>-dev` beside the suffixed version, and every rung
  and the closing build under the dev name, the closing over the bare version.
- **Land restores**: the rename back to `<name>` is Land's act, so the stable name is only ever
  installed from what `main` will carry.
- **A build script guards the pairing** on every cargo verb: a suffixed version under the stable
  name fails the build, so no mid-cycle install can clobber the consumers' binary.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change on **every commit**, so a built or
running artifact identifies the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project following the cycle protocol may bump
  less often: once per cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in [Recording the
  version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record) if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA,
  which a commit cannot contain.

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (opening -> commits -> closing, per the [Cycle protocol](../AGENTS.md#cycle-protocol))
encodes each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a
Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is not
a name for a step: a step is identified by its title, and an in-flight ladder rung carries neither a
number nor a version (see [Steps are named, not numbered](prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)).
The identifiers below count commits within a phase, and nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: the commits between
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle, with no ladder and no setup commit, skips `-0` and
starts at `-1` (its first commit). A single-step cycle is one commit, the Close-out, and carries the
bare `X.Y.Z` ([Cycle shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that grows a Preparation later adds the `0`
step without renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10`: commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a Preparation.
- `-1.0`: Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0`: Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2`: its commits between
- `X.Y.Z-3`: its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0`: Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of every step (the per-commit checklist carries the step),
so the manifest always records the commit it will be part of and, per the preference above, every
commit carries a distinct version.

# Cycle model

A cycle's `## In Progress` block, shown as a specimen rather than a skeleton: the `config loader`
cycle, mid-run, with its opening landed and its first work rung current. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [The In Progress block](notes.md#the-in-progress-block).

One thing the specimen cannot show:

- a single-step cycle drops both bookends and all the steps are in the one commit: the ladder is one
  unlinked rung with the bare title, and there are no rung subsections under it ([Cycle
  shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

## In Progress

### refactor: extract config loader

#### Problem

Config parsing lives inside the CLI entry point, so every subcommand that wants a setting reaches
through `main` for it, and a test cannot load a config without building the CLI.

#### Solution

Move config loading into its own module with a single `load` entry point that the CLI and the tests
call alike.

#### Acceptance check

`cargo test` passes with a new test that loads a config from a fixture file without touching `main`,
and `vc-x1 config --validate` reports the same findings as before the move.

#### Deliberation

- one work rung, not two: the parser and the loader were going to be split first and moved second,
  but the move is what forces the split, so doing them together is fewer edits
- the acceptance check compares `config --validate` output rather than asserting on internals, so a
  later rename inside the module does not invalidate it

#### Ladder

- [refactor: extract config loader opening][1] (done)
- [refactor: split loader from parser][2] (current)
- [refactor: extract config loader closing][3]

##### refactor: extract config loader opening

The cycle's setup commit: create and publish the bookmark, delete `## Closed`'s contents, move the
Todo entry into this block, and bump the version-of-record.

##### refactor: split loader from parser

Loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load without parsing and a test cannot parse
without a file on disk.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config/loader.rs` finds and reads the file, returning the text and its path, so a caller that
    only wants to know which file was read stops here.
  - `config/parser.rs` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands it a string and never
    touches the filesystem.
    - the error type stays shared for now, since splitting it would change the messages
      `config --validate` prints and the acceptance check compares them
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field access moves behind the module
    boundary and the CLI no longer knows the file's shape.

##### refactor: extract config loader closing

Closing out the cycle.

# References

[1]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-opening
[2]: #refactor-split-loader-from-parser
[3]: #refactor-extract-config-loader-closing

**Proposed title**

`docs: Todo plans init, delete, and rename`

The bookmark, from the title's slug, would be `docs-todo-plans-init-delete-and-rename`, created on `main` and published. That is a push, so it needs your go.

**Where the cycle-record goes**

The rules name `TODO.md > ## In Progress`. The last cycle kept its record in `zDOING.md` as a trial, and that bend covered that one cycle only. You said today you are not sure `zDOING.md` is right, so I don't want to assume either way:

- **`TODO.md`, as the rules say.** The block goes in `TODO.md > ## Closed`, and `zDOING.md` either keeps the sync cycle's record as a leftover or has it removed. This quietly ends the trial, which seems like more than a docs cycle should decide.

I'd continue the trial in `zDOING.md`, since it changes the least.

**What the one commit will carry**

- **Today's edits:** the `TODO.md` changes and the continuation notes reset in both files.
- **The record:** a short block written fresh, since no `## Todo` entry is being picked up. The ladder is the one unlinked rung with the bare title.

**Acceptance check I'd state**

`vc-x1 validate` passes, and `vc-x1 validate-anchors TODO.md` reports only the known false failure on the POR link.

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A session of planning left `TODO.md` holding a day of decisions as
uncommitted edits, with no cycle to carry them: what `vc-x1 delete` and `vc-x1 rename` are to do,
the order `init` is fixed in, and two faults the day turned up, commits no command reports and a
checker that reports a working link as broken.

#### Deliberation

- The cycle is single-step, wink's call: the edits were made in conversation, entry by entry, and
  the one commit is their record.
- The record is in this file, continuing the trial the last cycle began, wink's call at the
  opening.
  - It bends [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record) as that cycle's did: where the block is
    written and its order, and nothing else.
  - Whether this file and `zTODO.md` are the right ones is not settled, which is why
    `agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8` stays parked.
- No `## Todo` entry was picked up, so the block opens with the problem, where an entry's text
  would be.
- The order of `## Todo` is wink's: the two `validate-anchors` entries first, then `init`, delete,
  and rename, with the parked proposal after them.
- The checker's false failure is left standing and is the first entry's to fix. Taking the
  backticks out of the heading it trips on would pass the check today and lose the heading's
  mark of a command.
- The lock a running agent holds is planned as an experiment in this project's `custom.md`, with
  no `agent-files` proposal, wink's call. Nothing of it is in this cycle.
- The restore written for `sync --undo` was a draft under `tmp/` and is gone, wink having cleared
  `tmp/`. Its entry now says it is rewritten from the description.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, `vc-x1 closed` not landed and jj-lib offering no remote
  query, so nothing promotes.

#### Solution

`TODO.md` takes the day's planning in one commit.

- Two `validate-anchors` entries head `## Todo`: a new one for the slug of a heading holding a
  code span, and the cross-file check, moved up.
- The entry for `init`, delete, and rename follows, in the order they are to be done, with what
  stops the two commands and the lock a running agent holds.
- A new entry has `vc-x1 status` report the commits no bookmark reaches.
- The parked proposal's entry says why it stays parked, and the `sync --undo` entry that its
  draft is gone.
- The continuation notes are reset in both files, each fact acted on or filed.

#### Acceptance check

- `vc-x1 validate` passes.
- `vc-x1 validate-anchors TODO.md` reports one failure, the false one on the link to
  `#support-por-workspaces-in-push`, and no other.

#### Ladder

- docs: Todo plans init, delete, and rename (current)

'''

EOF

content.text:
Thoughts only, nothing edited. The cycle is still waiting at the work review.

**What you've described already half-exists.** `versioning.md` has a "lightweight cycle": no setup commit, the first commit carries the setup and the work at `-1`, and the close-out carries the bare version. Your shape is that, made the rule for small changes. So `-1` is the right suffix, since `-0` means a commit that is setup only.

**What it fixes**

- **One shape instead of two.** Every cycle would start and end the same way. The rule "Shape at the first push" and its escape hatch (re-titling a pushed single-step commit into an opening when the work grows) could go: a small cycle that grows just adds rungs before the close.
- **No rewrite at Land for the name.** Today a single-step commit is pushed as `vc-x1-dev` at a bare version, and Land restores the name by squashing into that already-pushed commit. In your shape the restore is a reviewed commit.
- **The acceptance check has something to check.** Today the one commit records its own check as passed before it exists. With a close commit, the check runs against the pushed work.
- **The record moves once, visibly.** The block sits in `## In Progress` while the work is reviewed and moves to `## Closed` at the close, as in a multi-step cycle.

**What it costs or breaks**

- **Double the ceremony for small changes.** Two validations, two reviews, two push approvals, then Land, where today there is one of each. For a change like today's, that is a lot.
- **More commits on `main`.** A ladder is never squashed, because each commit's `ochid:` trailer would be lost. So a small change lands as two commits kept separate, or three as a trapezoid.
- **Removing `-dev` in the close commit installs the real binary early.** Validation ends with `cargo install`, so validating the close commit under the plain name replaces your `vc-x1` before Land. The current rule has Land do the restore for exactly that reason: the stable name is only installed from what `main` will carry. If the final review sends the close back, you are running an unlanded build. This also differs from what multi-step cycles do today, so the two shapes would diverge again unless multi-step changes too.
- **Titles need a rule.** Two commits need two distinct titles. The bare title for the work commit and "closing" for the second would keep one `git log --grep` finding both.

**How I'd weigh it**

The one-shape simplification is the strongest argument, and it would shrink the agent-files. The early install is the one real fault; it goes away if the name restore stays at Land, as now, and the close commit only drops the version suffix.

**Whether it is a proposal**

It changes "Cycle shape", "Opening", "Close-out" and the suffix scheme, which are rules of the set, so making it permanent is an `agent-files` proposal. Trying it once is a bend you can grant for one cycle, recorded in that cycle's block.

**The current cycle** could be that trial. Only the bookmark has been pushed, and the shape is fixed at the first `vc-x1 push`, so it is still free to change. Otherwise it continues as the one-commit form now under review.

content.text:
Here is the full sequence as I'd write it, with your two changes applied. Thoughts only; nothing is edited and the current cycle is still at its work review.

## Open

1. **Bookmark:** create the bookmark on `main`, named by the title's slug, and publish it. No approval needed.
2. **Waiting:** check each `## Waiting` condition and promote what is met.
3. **Record:** delete what `## Closed` holds, and write the block in `## In Progress` with the rung marked `(current)`. The ladder has two rungs: the bare title and the title plus " closing".
4. **Name and version:** rename the artifact to `<name>-dev` and bump the version to `X.Y.Z-1`.
5. **Work:** do the work. Stop and ask on any deviation or question.
6. **Record the work:** write what changed into the block.
7. **Validate.**
8. **Work review:** stop with "please review" and iterate until your go.
9. **Describe:** mark the rung `(done)`, write the title and body, show them, and stop for approval to commit and push.
10. **Commit and push** to the bookmark with `vc-x1 push`, titled with the bare cycle title. Then stop.

## Close

1. **Acceptance check:** run it against the pushed work and record pass or fail.
2. **Name and version:** rename back to `<name>` and set the version to the bare `X.Y.Z`.
3. **Record:** finalize the block and move it whole to `## Closed`, leaving `## In Progress` reading `_No cycle currently in progress._`.
4. **Size:** add the line-count row if an agent-file changed.
5. **Validate**, the full run.
6. **Work review:** stop with "please review".
7. **Describe:** show the title and body, and stop for approval.
8. **Commit and push** to the bookmark, titled with the cycle title plus " closing". Then stop.

## Final review and Land

1. **Final review:** you look at the two commits on the bookmark and give the go to land.
2. **Fast-forward:** set `main` to the closing commit and push `main`. This is the only push to `main` in the cycle.
3. **Delete the bookmark,** locally and on the remote.
4. **Restart:** write any continuation notes, and you restart the agent.

## Choices I made in this

- **The name restore is in the close, as you listed it.** I leaned the other way last time, and I've changed my mind: by the close the work is already reviewed, and restoring at Land means squashing into a pushed commit. The consequence is that the close's validation installs the plain `vc-x1`, so the install is done before Land, not as part of it. If the final review sends the close back, you would be running an unlanded build until it is fixed.
- **The two commits land as they are, with no merge commit.** A trapezoid would add a third commit to `main` for a small change. `main` gets two commits from one push.
- **Approvals that remain:** the two `vc-x1 push` calls and the Land. The bookmark push at open and the bookmark deletion at Land are the only pushes without one. I assumed the deletion rides on the Land go; say if you want it asked separately.
- **Titles:** the bare title for the work commit and " closing" for the second, so one `git log --grep` finds both.

## Close-out shapes

The two shapes a ladder can land in, chosen by the user and recorded at close-out, executed at
[Land](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land) ([Close-out](../AGENTS.md#close-out)). A single-step cycle
is one commit and lands as it is:

- **trapezoid**, the current default: a merge commit whose first parent is the trunk and whose
  second is the ladder, so `git log --first-parent` reads one commit per cycle while every rung
  stays reachable. Reshaped at Land by the [recipe below](#trapezoid-close-out-recipe) and published
  by the landing fast-forward itself.
- **keep separate**, one commit per rung on `main`, when the decomposition itself is informative.

Squash is not a shape: each rung's `ochid:` trailer is a change id, a squash keeps one and drops the
rest, and every agent-repo commit that pointed at a dropped rung is left dangling ([Cycle
shape](../AGENTS.md#cycle-shape)).

**Preview before choosing.** The cycle's net change is the tree diff from `<base>` to the tip,
whatever shape the commits between are in: `jj diff --from <base> --to <tip>`, or the gitk range
described in [Read a change in gitk at full context](#read-a-change-in-gitk-at-full-context). The
trapezoid keeps each rung reachable while `git log --first-parent` shows this net diff once landed,
and keep separate shows the rungs themselves. The choice is made on what `main` will carry.

## Read a change in gitk at full context

gitk renders a change three ways, and at full context each answers a different question. Raise
"Lines of context" to the longest file's length, or to a large number such as 1000 (`--context 1000`
is the CLI equivalent), to see the entire file, then select:

- **New version**: the file as it now is, with the added lines lit. This is what the permanent
  branch will carry, so it is the view for judging whether a change reads as one thing.
- **Old version**: the file as it was, with the removed lines lit. It answers what the change costs,
  which a diff states only as minus lines out of context.
- **Diff**: the two interleaved. At full context it is the whole file with the edit marked in place,
  which is the reading a reviewer wants when the edit is small and the file is not.

The above reads one commit at a time and is useful. Another mode is to see how several commits
together changed the tree since a given `<base>` commit. To do that:

- Hover over the commit you want as the `<base>`, right click and select "Mark this commit".
- Hover over any commit above the `<base>`, right click and select "Diff marked commit -> this".

Now New version, Old version and Diff show the net change of everything between `<base>` and `this`.
If `<base>` is the parent of the `opening` commit and `this` is the `closing`, that is the cycle's
net change, and it can help you decide what shape to choose ([Close-out shapes](#close-out-shapes)).

## Trapezoid close-out recipe

The reshape behind the trapezoid shape, run at [Land](#cycle-bookmarks-create-and-land) step 2: the
close-out commit, pushed linearly by the closing rung, becomes a merge whose first parent is the
trunk line and whose second parent is the cycle's ladder. Nothing here publishes, the merge goes out
with Land's fast-forward.

```
  main line   ...--<base>------------------<closeout>--
                      \                    /
  ladder             <rung-1>--...--<tip>-+
```

- `<base>`: the **parent of the ladder's first rung**, the trunk position when the cycle opened. It
  becomes the first parent. Not always the previous close-out: a cycle landed linearly since
  (keep-separate shape, or a single-step cycle) sits on the trunk line and must stay there.
- `<tip>`: the cycle's last commit before the close-out. It becomes the second parent.
- `<closeout>`: the close-out commit, reshaped here.

1. `jj rebase -r <closeout> --onto <base> --onto <tip>`: `<closeout>` becomes the merge. Parent
   order is the argument order.
2. `jj new <closeout>`: an empty `@` above the merge. The bookmark followed the rewrite on its own.
   What step 1 leaves misplaced is the working copy: `jj rebase -r` re-parents descendants onto the
   rebased commit's old parent, so the empty `@` lands beside the merge on `<tip>` and the tree
   reverts to pre-close-out content, which looks alarming and is not.
3. Verify two parents: `jj log -r <closeout> -T 'parents.map(|p| p.change_id().short(8))'` must list
   both. jj preserves the second parent even though `<base>` is an ancestor of `<tip>` (observed at
   three consecutive close-outs), but a collapsed merge is indistinguishable from a correct one in
   `jj log --no-graph`.

Details:

- **Trailers survive.** The restore's squash and the reshape change `<closeout>`'s SHA but not its
  change id, so the `ochid:` trailers stamped at the closing push stay valid in both directions.
- **Immutability.** No flag is needed: a topic bookmark's commits are not on `trunk()` until Land's
  fast-forward.

Recovery:

- **Nothing is published until Land's fast-forward**, so the whole reshape is undoable with
  `jj undo` / `jj op restore`.
- **A collapsed or mis-parented merge**: undo and redo step 1 with the corrected revisions. Do not
  land a shape you did not intend. After the fast-forward the remote boundary is crossed and
  recovery is forward-only.
- **Working copy left beside the merge** (step 2 skipped): `jj new <closeout>` after the fact. Any
  commit made in the meantime branches off `<tip>` and needs a rebase onto the merge.

content.text:
Today a multi-step cycle does the two at different moments, and I agree the two shapes should match.

**What multi-step does now**

- **Version:** the closing commit sets the bare `X.Y.Z`. It is still built and validated under the `-dev` name at that point.
- **Name:** Land restores it. Land's first step renames `<name>-dev` back to `<name>`, runs `vc-x1 validate --fast` so the lockfile follows, and squashes that edit into the already-pushed closing commit. The rewritten closing commit goes out with the push of `main`.

So the name restore is never reviewed as a commit; it is folded in at Land. Trailers survive because the squash changes the commit's hash, not its change id.

**How that compares with the steps I listed**

My small-cycle steps put the name restore in the close commit, as your list did. That differs from multi-step today, so one of the two has to move.

**Option A: both restore the name at Land, as multi-step does now**

- The stable `vc-x1` is only ever installed from what `main` carries. This is the reason the rule gives.
- Land already rewrites the closing commit in a multi-step cycle to make the trapezoid merge, so one more fold costs nothing there.
- For the small cycle it means a pushed commit is rewritten at Land, and the restore is not seen in a review.

**Option B: both restore the name in the closing commit**

- The restore is reviewed like any other change, and Land stops editing files: it reshapes, pushes `main`, and deletes the bookmark.
- The closing's validation installs the plain `vc-x1` before Land. If the final review sends the closing back, you are running an unlanded build until it is fixed.
- The build guard still works, because the closing is the first commit where the bare version and the plain name appear together.

**My pick is A.** It is the smaller change: multi-step stays as it is, and the small cycle's close commit drops the version suffix only. The cost is the unreviewed rename, which is two lines in the manifest and lockfile.

With A, a small cycle and a multi-step cycle differ in one thing only: the number of rungs between the first commit and the closing. The first commit of a small cycle carries the setup and the work together at `-1`, where a multi-step cycle has a separate opening at `-0`.

uncommitted edits, with no cycle to carry them: what `vc-x1 delete` and `vc-x1 rename` are to do,

  the one commit is their record.

  opening.

    written and its order, and nothing else.
  - Whether this file and `zTODO.md` are the right ones is not settled, which is why
    `agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8` stays parked.

  would be.

message.content: I think one tweak, this is the opening, "## Closed" should remain the previous cycles information until we close "current" which replaces it. That's how mult-step should work too, I think? Thoughts only.

content.text:
Thoughts only, nothing edited.

**Yes, it would apply to multi-step too.** Today the rule is the opposite for both: Opening step 3 says to delete whatever `## Closed` holds before writing the new block, and the Cycle-record section says the closed block is "deleted by the next opening". Your tweak moves that deletion from the opening to the closing, where the new block replaces the old in one step.

**What it gains**

- **There is always a finished record in the file.** Today, from a cycle's opening to its closing, `## Closed` is empty and the last record is only in history. With the tweak the previous cycle stays readable until the moment its successor replaces it.
- **The opening's diff is only the new cycle.** It adds a block and no longer carries the removal of a few hundred lines about something else.
- **It matches what the old single-step shape already did.** Its one commit wrote straight into `## Closed`, replacing what was there.
- **The landmark is unchanged.** Each cycle's closing commit still holds that cycle's finished block in `## Closed`.

**What it costs**

- **Reference numbers collide.** This is the one real problem. Both blocks link their ladder rungs through numbered definitions in the file's `# References`, and each starts at 1. The sync record uses 1 to 5 and this cycle's uses 1. With both blocks in the file, the new one has to number on from the old (6 here) and the closing removes the old definitions with the old block. In `TODO.md`, where the rule says the record lives, the numbers are shared with the backlog's own references as well. The Todo entry "The opening deletes the closed block's reference definitions with it" would become the closing's job.
- **The closing's diff gets bigger.** It removes the old record and moves the new one, so the bookkeeping commit carries the large deletion the opening carries today. One commit has it either way.
- **The file holds two blocks during a cycle.** That is bounded, so "the file never grows" still holds, but two cycles with a same-titled rung would collide on anchors. That is rare.

**For this cycle**

I already removed the sync record from the working copy. Putting it back is easy, since it is in the parent commit, and this cycle's one reference would become 6. It would be a fifth bend for the trial, on the Cycle-record section, and I'd add it to the Deliberation.

I think the tweak is right: an empty `## Closed` for the whole length of a cycle is the weaker design, and the numbering is a small, mechanical cost.

content.text:
Partly: putting each block's definitions inside the block is a good idea, but the numbers cannot restart in each section.

**Why the numbers can't repeat**

Markdown reference definitions are global to the file, wherever they are written. If `[1]:` is defined under "References for In Progress" and again under "References for Closed", every `[1]` in the file resolves to the first definition. The closed block's ladder links would silently point at the running cycle's rungs.

**What your layout does solve**

- **A block carries its own definitions.** Moving the block from `## In Progress` to `## Closed` moves them with it, and deleting a block deletes them. That retires the Todo entry "The opening deletes the closed block's reference definitions with it".
- **The bottom `# References` holds only the file's own.** Nothing there belongs to a cycle, so nothing there needs cleaning at an opening or closing.

**How to make the labels unique**

- **Number on, as this cycle does.** The new block starts after the old one's last number. It works, but someone has to look up the old count, and the numbers drift upward until a reset.
- **Use the rung title as the label.** A label can be any text, not only a number. The rung becomes `- [feat: sync is safe by default opening] (done)` and its definition `[feat: sync is safe by default opening]: #feat-sync-is-safe-by-default-opening`. Titles are already required to be distinct within a cycle, and the bookends carry the cycle's own title, so two blocks cannot collide unless two cycles share a title. There is no number to maintain at all.

I'd take the title as the label. It fits "steps are named, not numbered", and the ladder reads the same as it does now minus the `[N]`.

**What it would need**

- **A rule change.** `notes.md` says the reference definitions are the file's last section, and the ladder form is written as `[<title>][M]`. Both would change, so it belongs with the proposal that makes the rest of this trial the rule.
- **A check of the tools.** I have not checked whether `vc-x1 validate-anchors` accepts a definition whose label is not a number, or one outside `# References`. If it does not, that is a small fix alongside the slug bug.
- **A long definition line.** A title of up to 50 characters plus its slug runs past 100 columns. The width rule already allows a line that reads better long.

**What it does not solve**

The four duplicate anchors from the repeated item headings (Deliberation, Solution, Acceptance check, Ladder) are a separate problem. Per-section references do not touch them.

content.text:
That would solve all three problems at once, and I think it is the cleanest of the options so far. Thoughts only; nothing is edited and the commit is still at its review.

**What a separate `zCLOSED.md` fixes**

- **Duplicate anchors go away.** The two blocks are in different files, so their Deliberation, Solution, Acceptance check and Ladder headings no longer collide. The Todo entry added a moment ago loses its motivating case, though it is still a fair fix for the checker.
- **Reference numbers restart at 1.** Each file has its own `# References`, so neither numbering on nor title labels is needed.
- **There is always a finished record.** The last cycle stays readable until the next closing, which is what your tweak was after.
- **The closing is one simple act.** The finished block and its references replace the whole content of `zCLOSED.md`, and `zDOING.md` goes back to its skeleton. Nothing has to be cut out from between other sections.
- **The opening never touches the old record.** Its diff is the new cycle alone.

**What it costs**

- **A third file.** It would sit beside `zDOING.md` and `zTODO.md`, and you are not yet sure about those two. Three files to hold what one file holds under the current rule is a real step.
- **`zDOING.md` is nearly empty between cycles.** It would hold the continuation notes and one line saying no cycle is in progress.
- **The closing's diff is a whole-file replacement.** The old record leaves and the new one arrives in the same file, so the diff shows both. That is the same content the closing would move anyway.

**What stays the same**

- **Links inside the block survive the move.** They are relative to the directory, and both files sit in the same one. The ladder's links to its own subsections stay within one file.
- **The landmark still works.** Each cycle's closing commit holds that cycle's finished block, now in `zCLOSED.md`.

**For this cycle**

It could be tried now: the sync record moves from `zDOING.md > ## Closed` into a new `zCLOSED.md` in this first commit, its references go with it as 1 to 5, and this cycle's reference goes back to 1. It would be one more item in the trial's Deliberation, replacing the two-blocks-in-one-file notes I wrote there.

# Doing: the cycle record

What is being done and what was just done: the running cycle's planning and its work's
documentation, and the last finished cycle's. What we might do is in [TODO.md](TODO.md). The
block's shape is on trial: it opens with the Todo as it was picked from `TODO.md`, then the
Deliberation, the plan, Solution and Acceptance check, and the Ladder with its details.

This file is a trial (2026-10-09). The agent-files still name `TODO.md > ## In Progress` as the
record's home, and the cycle that makes this file the rule is [The cycle-record moves out of
TODO.md into zDOING.md](TODO.md#the-cycle-record-moves-out-of-todomd-into-zdoingmd).

## Continuation notes

Where the agent was, for the agent that comes next. Ephemeral, never a record: read first, acted
on, and reset to `_None._` by the reader. Kept here by the trial, with a pointer to it under the
same heading in `TODO.md`, where [Acquaint](AGENTS.md#acquaint) still looks.

_None._

## In Progress

### docs: Todo plans init, delete, and rename

(wink + agent, 2026-10-11) A session of planning left `TODO.md` holding a day of decisions as
uncommitted edits, with no cycle to carry them: what `vc-x1 delete` and `vc-x1 rename` are to do,
the order `init` is fixed in, and two faults the day turned up, commits no command reports and a
checker that reports a working link as broken.

#### Deliberation

- The cycle is single-step, wink's call: the edits were made in conversation, entry by entry.
- The cycle is a trial of a new shape for a single-step cycle, wink's call at the work review of
  the one-commit form, before any `vc-x1 push`: two commits, the work and the closing, so a
  single-step cycle and a multi-step one differ in the rungs between and in nothing else.
  - The first commit carries the opening's duties and the work, under the dev name at the `-1`
    suffix, titled with the bare cycle title, the record in `## In Progress`.
  - The closing runs the acceptance check against the pushed work, sets the bare version, and
    moves the block to `## Closed`, titled with the cycle title and " closing".
  - The last cycle's record stays in `## Closed` until this one's closing replaces it, wink's
    call at the second work review, where the opening would have deleted it. There is then
    always a finished record in the file, and the opening's diff is its own cycle alone.
    - Two blocks share the file's reference definitions while the cycle runs, so this block's
      number on from the last one's, and the closing deletes the old definitions with the old
      block.
    - Two blocks also repeat the item headings, Deliberation, Solution, Acceptance check, and
      Ladder, and `vc-x1 validate-anchors` reports each second one as a duplicate anchor. Nothing
      links to them, and the four reports stand until the closing. The Todo entry
      [validate-anchors warns on a duplicate anchor only when a link names
      it](TODO.md#validate-anchors-warns-on-a-duplicate-anchor-only-when-a-link-names-it) is the
      fix.
    - Wink means it for a multi-step cycle too.
  - Land restores the plain name, as a multi-step cycle's does. Restoring it in the closing was
    weighed and left: the closing's validation would install the stable binary before `main`
    carries it.
  - The two commits land kept separate, with no merge commit, and `main` is pushed once.
  - The bookmark's create and publish needs no approval, wink's call. The two pushes and the
    Land keep theirs.
  - It bends [Cycle shape](AGENTS.md#cycle-shape), [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record),
    [Opening](AGENTS.md#opening), [Close-out](AGENTS.md#close-out), and [Before any
    push](AGENTS.md#before-any-push), for this cycle alone and as far as the bullets above say.
    Whether it becomes the rule is an `agent-files` proposal's to settle.
  - The first rung is unlinked and has no subsection: one headed by the bare title would collide
    with the title heading's anchor, and the Solution holds what it would say.
- The record is in this file, continuing the trial the last cycle began, wink's call at the
  opening.
  - It bends [Cycle-record](AGENTS.md#cycle-record) as that cycle's did: where the block is
    written and its order, and nothing else.
  - Whether this file and `zTODO.md` are the right ones is not settled, which is why
    `agent-files(proposal): v0.2.8` stays parked.
- No `## Todo` entry was picked up, so the block opens with the problem, where an entry's text
  would be.
- The order of `## Todo` is wink's: the `validate-anchors` entries first, then `init`, delete,
  and rename, with the parked proposal after them.
- The checker's false failure is left standing and is the first entry's to fix. Taking the
  backticks out of the heading it trips on would pass the check today and lose the heading's
  mark of a command.
- The lock a running agent holds is planned as an experiment in this project's `custom.md`, with
  no `agent-files` proposal, wink's call. Nothing of it is in this cycle.
- The restore written for `sync --undo` was a draft under `tmp/` and is gone, wink having cleared
  `tmp/`. Its entry now says it is rewritten from the description.
- The `## Waiting` conditions are unmet, `vc-x1 closed` not landed and jj-lib offering no remote
  query, so nothing promotes.

#### Solution

`TODO.md` takes the day's planning in one commit, and a closing follows it.

- Three `validate-anchors` entries head `## Todo`: a new one for the slug of a heading holding a
  code span, the cross-file check, moved up, and a new one for duplicate anchors no link names.

- The continuation notes are reset in both files, each fact acted on or filed.

- `vc-x1 validate-anchors TODO.md` reports one failure, the false one on the link to

136	### Commit-body form
137	
138	The specimen is [commit-model.md](commit-model.md). A commit body is the [Problem-first
139	shape](#problem-first-shape) with one addition: a body whose
140	problem has several sub-problems arranges them by a fixed recursion, so a reader knows what any
141	bullet is from its marker and its depth. The earlier statement, "a problem statement then a solution
142	statement, both broad", left that arrangement to taste, and taste converged slowly and separately.
143	
144	- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
145	  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
146	  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
147	  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
148	  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
149	- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
150	  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
151	  to be more than one commit.
152	- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
153	  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
154	  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
155	- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
156	  form, the general form at its smallest.
157	- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
158	  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
159	  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.
160	
161	**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
162	pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
163	typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
164	read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
165	flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
166	a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.
167	
168	Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
169	[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).
170	
171	### Semicolons
172	
173	Prose carries no semicolons. A semicolon appears only in code (code spans, fenced code, source
174	files), where it is syntax rather than prose. The structure a semicolon would have joined is written
175	explicitly instead:
176	
177	- **Two claims** take a period, each half standing as its own sentence ("The diff empties. The
178	  history keeps the record.").
179	- **A continuation** takes a comma with a conjunction, when one half carries the other's thought
180	  onward rather than making its own claim.
181	- **A list hiding in prose** (`A; B; C` inside a sentence or bullet) breaks into sub-bullets so the
182	  structure shows. List items that themselves contain commas restructure the same way rather than
183	  separating with semicolons.
184	
185	The code allowance is why a bare byte scan cannot enforce the rule: a checker blanks the code first,
186	then expects zero.
187	
188	The agent-files (`AGENTS.md`, `custom*`, `agent-data/*`) carry no historical exemption and are swept
189	to zero. Any other historical file keeps its existing semicolons only until it is touched: a commit
190	that edits a file makes that whole file's prose semicolons owed, code spans exempt, and the cycle
191	pays them in a penultimate rung of its own, or in its one commit when single-step, using the joins
192	above, so the touching rung's diff reads as its change alone. What is owed still follows from
193	touching the file, and only the payment moves. New prose is written correct and is never a sweep
194	item. A file whose count means rewriting rather than repunctuating becomes its own cycle. Files
195	outside a cycle's diff are never converted, since that is a sweep and sweeps are their own cycle.
196	Source-file comments are prose under this rule (see [code.md](code.md#comments-are-prose)).
197	
198	### Typeable punctuation only
199	
200	Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. The prohibition is on *authoring*,
201	not presence: a file may legitimately hold a banned character it transcribed (see below), so a byte
202	scan is not the rule and a sweep needs the authored/transcribed judgment. Banned from authoring:
203	`—`, `–`, `…`, `→`. None can be entered without a compose key or a paste, so none can be grepped
204	for, and an em dash next to option syntax reads as another flag. Like the semicolon rule above, the
205	agent-files are swept to zero and any other file converts whole when a cycle touches it, paid in
206	the same penultimate rung as the semicolons (specimens and transcriptions aside, below). A banned
207	character costs nothing to write and is paid on every read, so the rule is not softer than that.
208	
209	`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em dash
210	usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:
211	
212	- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
213	  sub-bullets.
214	- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a glossary
215	  or a command list at one line per entry.
216	- **A prose aside** takes a comma, parentheses, or two sentences. Often the aside should just go.
217	
218	Converting a heading moves its anchor. The em dash strips but the spaces on both sides survive, so
219	`## A — B` slugs to `#a--b` while its colon form slugs to `#a-b` (see [Markdown anchor
220	links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). Re-point inbound links in the same commit.
221	
222	Scope is the same as [Speculation marker](#speculation-marker), plus commit titles and everything
223	under `src/`: doc comments, inline comments, and any user-visible string. Source is the surface a
224	human edits and greps most, so an untypeable character costs more there than in prose. A code span
225	is not exempt by itself. Naming the character is a specimen and stays, which is how this section
226	names them. A banned character doing a job is a use and converts: `` `.expect(…)` `` becomes
227	`` `.expect(...)` ``.
228	
229	Text quoted from outside this repo's prose (tool output, an error message, an already-published
230	commit title) is transcribed, not written, so it keeps its characters, whether or not it sits in a
231	code span. It matters most for commit titles: converting one stops it matching `git log --grep` and
232	breaks the verbatim identity that [Conventional-commit
233	shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) requires between a commit title and its ladder
234	rung.

- **An intro paragraph states the general problem**, and defines any word the title assumes. It is
  mandatory. [Prose form](#prose-form) wants it regardless, and a body opening on a bullet is a body
  a `--body` flag can mistake for an option. The problem is *this commit's*, never the cycle's: the
  cycle's problem lives in the In Progress block, and a body whose problems outnumber what the diff
  resolves is describing something larger than the commit.
- **`*` bullets are the problem's facets**: sub-problems that decompose the intro's general problem,
  not a grab-bag of unrelated fixes. A body reaching for unrelated problem bullets is usually asking
  to be more than one commit.
- **`-` bullets are solutions**, and every `-` sits under a `*`, solving that facet. A `-` with no
  `*` above it reads as a solution to nothing, so there are no top-level solutions: a solution that
  retires every facet at once is written under each, or the facets are one.
- **One facet is the trivial commit**: the intro, one `*`, one or more `-` under it. Not a second
  form, the general form at its smallest.
- **A bookend body is a pointer**: an opening or closing commit resolves no problem of its own, so
  its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the cycle by its title and pointing at its record,
  the In Progress block. No `*`, no `-`.

**The markers are typed on purpose**: `*` always means problem, `-` always means solution, and the
pairing is what a reader counts on: the `-` answers the `*` above it, with no rule to consult. The
typing also keeps history greppable (`^\* ` finds every facet, `^ - ` every solution). Bodies are
read as plain text, in `jj log` and in terminals, where the markers survive, and if a renderer ever
flattens them the indentation still carries the structure. So the mixed markers are deliberate, and
a linter's consistent-marker rule is wrong to normalize them.

Unchanged by this: no version in title or body, no file list, no deliberation, titles per
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit).

### Semicolons

Prose carries no semicolons. A semicolon appears only in code (code spans, fenced code, source
files), where it is syntax rather than prose. The structure a semicolon would have joined is written
explicitly instead:

- **Two claims** take a period, each half standing as its own sentence ("The diff empties. The
  history keeps the record.").
- **A continuation** takes a comma with a conjunction, when one half carries the other's thought
  onward rather than making its own claim.
- **A list hiding in prose** (`A; B; C` inside a sentence or bullet) breaks into sub-bullets so the
  structure shows. List items that themselves contain commas restructure the same way rather than
  separating with semicolons.

The code allowance is why a bare byte scan cannot enforce the rule: a checker blanks the code first,
then expects zero.

The agent-files (`AGENTS.md`, `custom*`, `agent-data/*`) carry no historical exemption and are swept
to zero. Any other historical file keeps its existing semicolons only until it is touched: a commit
that edits a file makes that whole file's prose semicolons owed, code spans exempt, and the cycle
pays them in a penultimate rung of its own, or in its one commit when single-step, using the joins
above, so the touching rung's diff reads as its change alone. What is owed still follows from
touching the file, and only the payment moves. New prose is written correct and is never a sweep
item. A file whose count means rewriting rather than repunctuating becomes its own cycle. Files
outside a cycle's diff are never converted, since that is a sweep and sweeps are their own cycle.
Source-file comments are prose under this rule (see [code.md](code.md#comments-are-prose)).

### Typeable punctuation only

Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. The prohibition is on *authoring*,
not presence: a file may legitimately hold a banned character it transcribed (see below), so a byte
scan is not the rule and a sweep needs the authored/transcribed judgment. Banned from authoring:
`—`, `–`, `…`, `→`. None can be entered without a compose key or a paste, so none can be grepped
for, and an em dash next to option syntax reads as another flag. Like the semicolon rule above, the
agent-files are swept to zero and any other file converts whole when a cycle touches it, paid in
the same penultimate rung as the semicolons (specimens and transcriptions aside, below). A banned
character costs nothing to write and is paid on every read, so the rule is not softer than that.

`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em dash
usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:

- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
  sub-bullets.
- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a glossary
  or a command list at one line per entry.
- **A prose aside** takes a comma, parentheses, or two sentences. Often the aside should just go.

Converting a heading moves its anchor. The em dash strips but the spaces on both sides survive, so
`## A — B` slugs to `#a--b` while its colon form slugs to `#a-b` (see [Markdown anchor
links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). Re-point inbound links in the same commit.

Scope is the same as [Speculation marker](#speculation-marker), plus commit titles and everything
under `src/`: doc comments, inline comments, and any user-visible string. Source is the surface a
human edits and greps most, so an untypeable character costs more there than in prose. A code span
is not exempt by itself. Naming the character is a specimen and stays, which is how this section
names them. A banned character doing a job is a use and converts: `` `.expect(…)` `` becomes
`` `.expect(...)` ``.

Text quoted from outside this repo's prose (tool output, an error message, an already-published
commit title) is transcribed, not written, so it keeps its characters, whether or not it sits in a
code span. It matters most for commit titles: converting one stops it matching `git log --grep` and
breaks the verbatim identity that [Conventional-commit
shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--commit) requires between a commit title and its ladder
rung.

# Commit model

Two commit bodies from the `config loader` cycle in [cycle-model.md](cycle-model.md), shown as
specimens rather than a skeleton: a work rung's body and a bookend's. Copy the shape, not the
words. The rules are in [Commit-body form](prose.md#commit-body-form).

## A work rung

Title: `refactor: split loader from parser`

```
Config loading and parsing are one function, so the CLI cannot load a
config without parsing it and a test cannot parse one without a file on
disk. The move into its own module is what forces the split.

* The two jobs share one function and one error type.
  - `config::loader` finds and reads the file and returns the text with
    its path, so a caller that only wants to know which file was read
    stops there.
  - `config::parser` takes text and returns the schema, so a test hands
    it a string and never touches the filesystem.
* `main` still reaches into the parse result by field.
  - `main` calls `config::load` and receives the schema, so the field
    access moves behind the module boundary and the CLI no longer knows
    the file's shape.
```

The intro states this commit's problem and defines "split", the word the title assumes. Each `*`
is one facet of it, each `-` under a `*` answers that facet, and nothing names a file that the
diff already lists.

## A bookend

Title: `refactor: extract config loader opening`

```
Opens the cycle "refactor: extract config loader". Its record is the
In Progress block in TODO.md.
```

A bookend resolves no problem of its own, so its body is the intro paragraph alone, naming the
cycle by its title and pointing at its record. The closing's body is the same shape with "Closes".

A day of planning sat in TODO.md as uncommitted edits with no cycle to
carry them, and the cycle that carries them is itself a trial of how a
single-step cycle runs. "Plans" means the backlog's entries for work not
yet started: what is to be built, in what order, and what is undecided.

* Nothing renames or removes a workspace, and init fails on a template
  that is itself a workspace.
  - One entry plans the init fixes, then `vc-x1 delete`, then
    `vc-x1 rename`, in that order, with what stops the two commands and
    the lock a running agent holds.
* The anchor checker reports a working link as broken, and commits no
  bookmark reaches are shown by no command.
  - Three validate-anchors entries head the list: the slug of a heading
    holding a code span, the cross-file check, and duplicate anchors no
    link names.
  - A new entry has `vc-x1 status` report the commits no bookmark
    reaches.
* Two entries and the continuation notes were stale.
  - The parked proposal's entry says why it stays parked, the
    `sync --undo` entry says its draft is gone, and the notes are reset.
* A single-step cycle is one commit that records its own acceptance
  check, and its opening deletes the last finished record.
  - This cycle runs as two commits, the work and a closing, with its
    record in zDOING.md.
  - The last cycle's record moves to a file of its own, zCLOSED.md, and
    stays there until this cycle's closing replaces it.
